docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The purpose of this block diagram is to show the overall electrical layout of my subsystem and how the different components will interact. It shows the power levels used throughout the system, the optical slot sensor and op-amp circuit used for sensing, and the motor and motor driver circuits used as actuators. The diagram also shows how these components connect to the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano and which microcontroller pins and peripherals are being used. Finally, it shows the ribbon cable connections that allow my subsystem to communicate with the other team members' boards and the power sources needed to operate the system.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The purpose of this component selection assignment is to research and compare different electrical and electromechanical components for my subsystem of Team 101's Automatic Pet Food Dispenser.

My subsystem includes an optical slot sensor, op-amp filter circuit, MOSFET, motor, H-bridge motor driver, and power regulation circuitry. Each major component will be evaluated based on electrical specifications, compatibility, cost, ease of implementation, and suitability for the overall design.

The system uses the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano microcontroller. The control circuitry will use regulated 5V power where appropriate, while the motor will use a separate power supply based on its voltage and current requirements.

docs.title: 1. DC Motor
docs.text:
Subsystem: Food Dispensing Mechanism

The DC motor provides the mechanical motion required to operate the Automatic Pet Food Dispenser. The motor will rotate the dispensing mechanism to release food in controlled amounts.

A 12V geared DC motor is preferred because it provides useful torque, a manageable rotational speed, and a larger mechanical structure suitable for moving the dispensing mechanism.

The motor selection is based on operating voltage, speed, torque, physical size, current requirements, cost, and compatibility with the motor driver.

docs.title: Component Comparison
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Option 1: DFRobot FIT0492-B 12V Metal Gearmotor Manufacturer: DFRobot  Part Number: FIT0492-B  Operating Voltage: 12V  No-Load Speed: 100 RPM  Rated Torque: 686.5 mN·m (approximately 7 kg·cm)  Gear Ratio: 100:1  Motor Diameter: 37 mm  Output Shaft: 6 mm  Price: $11.90  DigiKey Product Datasheet - 12V operation is compatible with our proposed power system.  - 100 RPM provides a reasonable speed for controlled dispensing.  - Metal gearbox provides increased output torque.  - Rated torque of approximately 7 kg·cm is suitable for consideration in a mechanical dispensing system.  - Larger 37 mm motor provides a more substantial mechanical design.  - 6 mm shaft allows connection to the dispensing mechanism.  - Lower price than many comparable geared motors.  - Available through DigiKey. - Requires a separate motor driver capable of handling the motor current.  - Stall current must be verified before selecting the H-bridge.  - Larger motor requires more mounting space.  - Requires a suitable mounting bracket and shaft coupler. Option 2: DFRobot FIT0492-A 12V Metal Gearmotor Manufacturer: DFRobot  Part Number: FIT0492-A  Operating Voltage: 12V  No-Load Speed: 50 RPM  Rated Torque: 883 mN·m (approximately 9 kg·cm)  Motor Diameter: 37 mm  Price: $11.90  DigiKey Product Datasheet - Higher rated torque than the FIT0492-B.  - Slower rotation may improve dispensing control.  - Metal gearbox is suitable for mechanical actuation.  - Compatible with a 12V supply.  - Same listed price as the FIT0492-B.  - Available through DigiKey. - Slower speed may increase dispensing time.  - Requires additional mechanical mounting space.  - Stall current must be checked before selecting the motor driver.  - Higher torque may not be necessary for our dispensing mechanism. Option 3: Seeed Studio 114090046 DC Gearmotor Manufacturer: Seeed Technology  Part Number: 114090046  Operating Voltage: 6V–12V  Rated Torque: 137.3 mN·m (approximately 1.4 kg·cm)  Price: $5.20  DigiKey Product Datasheet - Lowest price among the three options.  - Supports operation within a 6V–12V range.  - Suitable for lightweight mechanical movement.  - Can operate from the proposed 12V motor supply if permitted by the manufacturer's specifications. - Much lower rated torque than the DFRobot motors.  - May not provide sufficient force to move the food dispensing mechanism.  - Speed is not specified in the referenced DigiKey listing.  - Less suitable for a larger dispensing mechanism.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
The DFRobot FIT0492-B 12V Metal Gearmotor is selected for our Automatic Pet Food Dispenser because it provides a good balance of rotational speed, output torque, mechanical size, and cost.

The motor operates at 12V and has a no-load speed of approximately 100 RPM. This speed makes it a reasonable candidate for rotating the dispensing mechanism at a controlled rate.

The motor also provides a rated torque of approximately 7 kg·cm, making it a promising option for moving a mechanical dispensing system. The metal gearbox increases the available output torque while reducing rotational speed.

Compared with the DFRobot FIT0492-A, the selected motor provides a higher rotational speed while maintaining substantial rated torque. This may allow food to be dispensed more quickly without requiring an excessively fast motor.

Compared with the Seeed Studio 114090046, the FIT0492-B provides significantly greater rated torque, making it a more suitable candidate for a larger dispensing mechanism.

Another advantage is the motor's price of approximately $11.90, which is lower than many comparable geared DC motors. It is also listed through DigiKey, allowing us to maintain consistency with our other component selections.

The 37 mm motor diameter and 6 mm output shaft make it suitable for integration into the mechanical dispensing assembly.

Therefore, the DFRobot FIT0492-B is our preferred DC motor because it provides a useful combination of speed, torque, mechanical strength, and affordability.

docs.title: 2. H-Bridge Motor Driver
docs.text:
Subsystem: DC Motor Direction and Speed Control

The H-bridge motor driver will control the direction and speed of the DC motor used in our Automatic Pet Food Dispenser. The driver will receive control signals from the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano and deliver power to the motor.

Our selected motor is the DFRobot FIT0492-B 12V metal gearmotor. Therefore, the H-bridge must support a 12V motor supply, provide sufficient output current, and operate with the microcontroller's control signals.

The selection criteria include operating voltage, output current, protection features, ease of PCB integration, component availability, and compatibility with our existing schematic.

docs.title: Component Comparison
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Option 1: Fairchild FAN8100N Manufacturer: Fairchild Semiconductor  Part Number: FAN8100N  Motor Supply: 1.8V–9V  Peak Current: 1.5A per channel  Package: 12-DIP  DigiKey Product Datasheet - Already used in our previous KiCad schematic.  - Through-hole package is easy to solder.  - Integrated motor driver reduces external circuitry.  - Supports low-voltage control applications. - Maximum recommended motor supply is only 9V.  - Cannot safely operate our selected 12V motor at its rated voltage.  - Limited output current compared with newer drivers.  - Obsolete component is less suitable for a new design. Option 2: Texas Instruments DRV8876PWPR Manufacturer: Texas Instruments  Part Number: DRV8876PWPR  Motor Supply: 4.5V–37V  Peak Output Current: 3.5A  Package: 16-HTSSOP  Price: $2.07 each  DigiKey Product Datasheet - Supports 12V motor operation.  - Compatible with 3.3V and 5V logic inputs.  - Integrated current sensing and regulation.  - Includes overcurrent and thermal protection.  - Supports PWM speed control and bidirectional motor operation. - Lower peak current than the DRV8874.  - May be unsuitable if the selected motor has a high stall current.  - Surface-mount package is harder to solder manually.  - Requires PCB layout and thermal design considerations. Option 3: Texas Instruments DRV8874PWPR Manufacturer: Texas Instruments  Part Number: DRV8874PWPR  Motor Supply: 4.5V–37V  Peak Output Current: 6A  Package: 16-HTSSOP  DigiKey Product Manufacturer Datasheet - Supports our selected 12V motor supply.  - Higher 6A peak current capability than the DRV8876.  - Compatible with 3.3V and 5V microcontroller logic.  - Integrated current sensing and current regulation.  - Includes overcurrent, undervoltage, and thermal protection.  - Supports PWM speed control and motor direction control.  - Integrated H-bridge reduces the need for external switching MOSFETs. - Surface-mount package requires careful soldering.  - Thermal pad requires appropriate PCB copper and vias.  - More complicated PCB layout than a through-hole driver.  - 6A is a peak rating, not a guaranteed continuous current capability.  - Motor stall current must still be verified.

docs.title: Final Selection
docs.text:
Selected Component: Option 3 – Texas Instruments DRV8874PWPR

Manufacturer: Texas Instruments

Manufacturer Part Number: DRV8874PWPR

Motor Driver Type: Integrated Brushed DC H-Bridge

Operating Supply Voltage: 4.5V–37V

Planned Motor Supply: 12V DC

Peak Output Current: 6A

Control Logic: Supports 3.3V and 5V inputs

Control Methods: PWM, Phase/Enable, Independent Half-Bridge

Package: 16-HTSSOP

Supplier: DigiKey

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
The Texas Instruments DRV8874PWPR is selected as the preferred H-bridge motor driver for our Automatic Pet Food Dispenser because it supports 12V motor operation, offers a relatively high peak output current, and includes integrated protection features.

The DRV8874 operates from a motor supply between 4.5V and 37V, making it compatible with the proposed 12V power system.

Its 6A peak output current capability provides greater potential current-handling capacity than the DRV8876, although the selected motor's actual stall current must still be verified.

The DRV8874 also supports 3.3V and 5V logic inputs, allowing it to interface with the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano without requiring 12V control signals.

The integrated H-bridge allows the microcontroller to control motor direction and speed through digital control signals and PWM.

Another important advantage is the integrated current sensing and current regulation. These features can help detect excessive motor loading and reduce the risk of damage during startup or mechanical jams.

Compared with the FAN8100N used in our previous KiCad schematic, the DRV8874 supports the higher motor supply voltage required by our new 12V motor.

Compared with the DRV8876, the DRV8874 provides a higher peak output current rating and lower combined high-side and low-side MOSFET on-resistance.

Therefore, the DRV8874PWPR is our preferred H-bridge motor driver, pending verification of the motor's stall current, driver thermal performance, and final PCB layout.

docs.title: 3. Linear Voltage Regulator
docs.text:
Subsystem: 5V Power Regulation

The linear voltage regulator will convert the main DC power supply voltage into a stable 5V output for compatible electronic components in the Automatic Pet Food Dispenser.

Our existing KiCad schematic already includes an LM7805 voltage regulator, barrel jack, and filtering capacitors. Reusing this design will reduce the changes required for our upcoming schematic assignment.

The final power system is planned to use a 12V DC input. The motor will operate from the 12V supply through the H-bridge driver, while the linear regulator will provide 5V for compatible low-power control circuitry.

docs.title: Component Comparison
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Option 1: Texas Instruments LM7805CT/NOPB Manufacturer: Texas Instruments  Part Number: LM7805CT/NOPB  DigiKey Part Number: 296-47192-ND  Output Voltage: 5V  Maximum Input Voltage: 35V  Rated Output Current: 1.5A  Package: TO-220-3  Price: $1.86  DigiKey Product Datasheet - Produces a regulated 5V output.  - Compatible with a 12V input supply.  - Supports up to 1.5A under appropriate thermal conditions.  - Includes overcurrent and thermal protection.  - Through-hole package simplifies assembly.  - Matches the LM7805 regulator family already used in our KiCad schematic. - Generates heat because excess voltage is dissipated as power.  - May require a heatsink at higher output currents.  - Less efficient than a switching regulator.  - Listed as temporarily out of stock at DigiKey during research. Option 2: STMicroelectronics L7805CV Manufacturer: STMicroelectronics  Part Number: L7805CV  DigiKey Part Number: 497-1443-5-ND  Output Voltage: 5V  Maximum Input Voltage: 35V  Rated Output Current: 1.5A  Package: TO-220  Price: $1.08  DigiKey Product Datasheet - Regulated 5V output.  - Compatible with a 12V input.  - Rated for up to 1.5A with adequate cooling.  - Through-hole package is easy to solder.  - Lower price than the Texas Instruments option.  - Widely available through DigiKey. - Generates heat during voltage conversion.  - May require a heatsink.  - Requires checking capacitor values and pin configuration before substituting.  - Would require updating the manufacturer part number in our schematic. Option 3: onsemi MC7805CTG Manufacturer: onsemi  Part Number: MC7805CTG  DigiKey Part Number: MC7805CTGOS-ND  Output Voltage: 5V  Maximum Input Voltage: 35V  Rated Output Current: 1A  Package: TO-220  Price: $1.01  DigiKey Product Datasheet - Produces a stable 5V output.  - Supports 12V input operation.  - Through-hole package simplifies PCB assembly.  - Lower cost than the other candidates.  - Available through DigiKey. - Lower rated output current than the other options.  - Generates heat when converting 12V to 5V.  - Requires checking the footprint and pinout before substitution.  - May require additional cooling depending on current consumption.

Input Voltage: Up to 35V

Rated Output Current: 1.5A (subject to thermal limitations)

Package: TO-220-3 (Through-Hole)

Unit Price: $1.86

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
The Texas Instruments LM7805CT/NOPB is selected for our Automatic Pet Food Dispenser because it provides a regulated 5V output and is compatible with the LM7805 regulator circuit already created in our previous KiCad assignment.

The regulator supports input voltages up to 35V, allowing it to operate from our proposed 12V DC supply. Its fixed 5V output is suitable for powering compatible sensor and signal-conditioning circuits, including our selected MCP6004 op-amp.

The LM7805CT/NOPB has a rated output current of 1.5A under appropriate thermal conditions. This provides potential current capacity for our low-power electronics, although the actual usable current will depend on heat dissipation and the final power budget.

Compared with the STMicroelectronics L7805CV and onsemi MC7805CTG, the Texas Instruments regulator offers similar basic voltage regulation capabilities. The main reason for selecting it is compatibility with our existing LM7805-based schematic and its established electrical specifications.

The TO-220 through-hole package is also convenient for PCB assembly and allows a heatsink to be added if necessary.

Therefore, the Texas Instruments LM7805CT/NOPB is our preferred linear voltage regulator, allowing us to reuse much of our existing power regulation circuit.

docs.title: 4. External Power Supply
docs.text:
Subsystem: Main DC Power Supply

The external power supply will convert AC electricity from a standard wall outlet into regulated 12V DC power for our Automatic Pet Food Dispenser.

The selected power supply must plug directly into a standard US wall outlet without requiring a separate AC power cord. It must also provide sufficient current to operate the 12V DC motor, H-bridge motor driver, and low-voltage electronics.

Our selected DFRobot FIT0492-B motor operates at 12V. The DRV8874 H-bridge motor driver will control the motor, while the LM7805 linear voltage regulator will convert 12V into 5V for compatible electronic components.

docs.title: Component Comparison
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Option 1: MEAN WELL SGA60U12-P1J Manufacturer: MEAN WELL  Part Number: SGA60U12-P1J  Output Voltage: 12V DC  Output Current: 5A  Output Power: 60W  Type: Wall-Mount AC/DC Adapter  Plug: US Wall Plug  Price: $27.79 each  DigiKey Product Manufacturer Information - Provides regulated 12V DC power.  - Supplies up to 5A and 60W.  - Plugs directly into a standard US wall outlet.  - No separate AC power cord required.  - Suitable for powering a 12V motor system. - More expensive than some alternative adapters.  - Larger wall-mounted adapter may block nearby outlets.  - Connector compatibility must be verified.  - Motor stall current must still be checked. Option 2: TT Electronics PSAW65I-12-B1 Manufacturer: TT Electronics / Power Partners  Part Number: PSAW65I-12-B1  Output Voltage: 12V DC  Output Current: 5A  Output Power: 60W  Type: Wall-Mount AC/DC Adapter  Plug: US Wall Plug  Price:  $21.59 (verify before purchase)  DigiKey Product Search Datasheet - Provides the required 12V DC output.  - Supplies up to 5A of current.  - Plugs directly into a standard US wall outlet.  - Does not require a separate AC power cord.  - Provides up to 60W of output power.  - Convenient for a compact pet food dispenser.  - Reasonable estimated price. - Larger than lower-power wall adapters.  - May block an adjacent wall outlet.  - Barrel connector dimensions and polarity must be verified.  - Motor startup and stall current must be checked against the supply rating. Option 3: Adafruit Industries 4880 Manufacturer: Adafruit Industries  Part Number: 4880  Output Voltage: Adjustable, 3V–12V DC  Maximum Output Current: 5A  Maximum Output Power at 12V: 60W  Type: External AC/DC Desktop Adapter  AC Connection: US Wall Plug with Cord  DC Connector: 5.5mm OD × 2.1mm ID Barrel Plug  Polarity: Center Positive  Price: $17.50  DigiKey Product - Available from DigiKey.  - Supports 12V operation.  - Provides up to 5A of current.  - Uses a common center-positive barrel connector.  - Adjustable output voltage provides flexibility.  - Lower listed price than our selected adapter. - Does not plug directly into the outlet as a single wall-mounted unit.  - Adjustable voltage must be set correctly to avoid damaging components.  - Motor stall current must still be verified.  - Less convenient than our selected fixed-voltage wall adapter.

docs.text:
Selected Component: Option 2 – TT Electronics PSAW65I-12-B1

Manufacturer: TT Electronics / Power Partners

Manufacturer Part Number: PSAW65I-12-B1

Power Supply Type: Wall-Mount AC/DC Adapter

Output Voltage: 12V DC

Maximum Output Current: 5A

Maximum Output Power: 60W

AC Connection: Direct US Wall Plug

Unit Price: $21.59

Supplier: DigiKey

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
The TT Electronics PSAW65I-12-B1 is selected as the preferred external power supply for our Automatic Pet Food Dispenser because it provides the required 12V DC output while plugging directly into a standard US wall outlet.

Unlike desktop power adapters that require a separate AC power cord, this wall-mounted adapter provides a simpler and more convenient power connection.

The adapter has a rated output of 12V at 5A, allowing it to provide up to 60W of electrical power.

Our selected DFRobot FIT0492-B motor operates at 12V, so this supply is compatible with the planned motor voltage.

The 12V output will be connected to the PCB through a barrel jack. The power will then be distributed to the DRV8874 H-bridge motor driver and the LM7805 linear voltage regulator.

The DRV8874 will control motor direction and speed, while the LM7805 will provide a regulated 5V output for compatible sensors and signal-conditioning components.

Compared with the MEAN WELL SGA60U12-P1J, the TT Electronics adapter offers a similar 12V, 5A output rating at a potentially lower price.

Compared with the GE60I12-P1J, the TT Electronics adapter uses a direct US wall-plug configuration without requiring an interchangeable AC plug attachment.
